scope: Execute checked Entity and Value Object factories through create, reconstruct, Entity transition and declared extension chains. Reuse the shared source lifecycle requests and independent whole-source owned observer without changing generated runtimes.
reference: Preserve every shared lifecycle request, Rule failure, validator order, invalid previous/fields precedence, identity-change result, optional omission, extension failure and exhaustive bounded extension permutation. Bind validator traces to current source closures and actual Python module hashes. Unsatisfied witnesses or case/chain capacity keep the whole factory not_evaluable, not a passing subset.
representation: Compare semantic views, trace outcomes and native/source key equivalence classes, not TypeScript-specific metadata or key bytes. Python snapshots, fields, results, traces, validators, collections, factories and extension tuples retain their native immutable/nominal contracts. Entity equality uses identity, Value Object equality uses all fields. JS frozen and null-prototype field inputs transport as exact inert Python dictionaries, not a promise to accept mapping subclasses; accessor/non-enumerable/inherited negatives transport as hostile subclasses and must not be accessed.
execution: Check fresh snapshots and factory extensions, unchanged inputs/previous snapshots/base factories, stable keys and equal hashes, no source identity collapse or splitting, foreign/clone rejection, constructor guards and exact native errors. Compile and reject two independent return/effect substitutions for each factory. Reuse the pinned owned recipe runtime for nested values and factory construction witnesses.
integration: Preserve single-workspace and bounded-stdin execution, total case/byte/process limits and final source/toolchain/workspace/cleanup invalidation. Keep all other metatypes and formal/cross-generator obligations explicit. No public CLI default, database operation, product policy, admission or release changes.
claim_ceiling: Bounded source-directed native lifecycle verification, not universal proof, arbitrary Python isolation, external persistence or full CLI completion. Native exception shields retain prior generator regression evidence; source-pure Rules cannot manufacture ambient exceptions.
